_description: Hand-maintained snapshot of the AWS actions actually usable by the read-only role this agent runs as (docs/context.md section 8) — 'actions' below means empirically verified working (a real AWS call was made and did not return AccessDenied), not merely present in the role's identity-based policy; see _blocked_by_permissions_boundary for why that distinction matters here. This is NOT the same thing as iam/policy.json: policy.json is our own hand-authored, aspirational least-privilege ask (kept in exact sync with what the registry/dispatch code uses, via tests/test_iam_drift.py). This file describes an external fact instead — the role was provisioned by whoever administers the sandbox account, we don't control its contents, and it grants a different (overlapping but distinct) set of actions than what our code was designed against. Kept in sync by hand whenever the real role changes; used by agent/permissions.py to decline a capability before ever attempting its AWS call, instead of discovering the gap via AccessDenied.

_blocked_by_permissions_boundary.note: Discovered 2026-08-06 during a full test pass, the same way the CI role's own permissions-boundary requirement was discovered (docs/context.md section 7.6, ci/runbook.md) — a separate policy (arn:aws:iam::767398067510:policy/intern-permissions-boundary) attached to this role too, capping what its identity-based policy grants. These four actions ARE present in the role's identity-based policy (an earlier version of this file listed them as granted on that basis alone) but every one of them returns AccessDenied/AccessDeniedException with an explicit 'no permissions boundary allows the <action> action' message when actually called — confirmed directly, not assumed, and distinguished from a legitimate resource-not-found response (verified s3:ListBucket/s3:GetBucketPolicyStatus/eks:DescribeCluster all return real NoSuchBucket/ResourceNotFoundException instead, i.e. the action itself is permitted, only the specific resource wasn't). Consequence: both of dispatch's CloudWatch Logs capabilities (agent/dispatch.py's count-only logs:FilterLogEvents and the plain logs:DescribeLogGroups entry) are built, unit-tested against moto, and allow-listed, but currently non-functional against this real account — the agent still answers gracefully (agent/router.py's reactive AccessDenied handling, docs/context.md section 8) rather than crashing or lying, but moving these out of 'actions' here lets the proactive gate catch it before wasting a real AWS call, which is more accurate and more efficient than relying on that reactive fallback alone.

_blocked_by_missing_identity_grant.note: Discovered 2026-08-07 while investigating the permissions-boundary gap above: ecr:DescribeRepositories is NOT blocked by intern-permissions-boundary (confirmed against the real boundary policy text — it explicitly allows both ecr:DescribeRepositories and ecr:CreateRepository), but this role's own identity-based policy (CloudOpsCopilotReadOnly) never grants it at all — only ECR push-side actions the CI/CD role's pipeline needs (PutImage, BatchGetImage, GetAuthorizationToken, etc., see _excluded_from_agent_use below). Confirmed directly: AccessDeniedException explicitly says 'no identity-based policy allows the ecr:DescribeRepositories action', the opposite wording from a boundary denial ('no permissions boundary allows...'). Consequence: agent/dispatch.py's ecr describe_repositories ALLOWLIST entry (built and unit-tested against moto) is currently non-functional against this real account for a different reason than the boundary-blocked actions above — the fix needed is a one-action addition to the role's own identity policy, not the boundary.

_excluded_from_agent_use.note: This role's attached policy also grants these ECR write/push actions. CloudCopilot's own agent code never calls any ecr:* operation — no registry entry or dispatch allow-list entry references the ecr service at all — a separate, dedicated role is used for the CI/CD pipeline's image push instead (docs/context.md section 7.6). Listed here only so this file honestly reflects the role's full real grant, not a convenient subset of it.
